newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end up in quiet pre-jobs trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end up in quiet pre-jobs trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished higher in quiet trading before Friday's key jobs report.
Activity was slim as many players took to the sidelines before the key March jobs number. Traders said local short-covering buoyed June T-bonds in afternoon trade.
U.S. March non-farm payrolls were forecast to rise 196,000, compared with a 339,000 gain in February. The jobless rate was seen edging down to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent.
"My comment is about three lines today," said Kurt Fraim, futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston. "We opened, we closed, and good luck tomorrow," he said.

"It's very rangebound and very consolidative before tomorrow's numbers," agreed Holly Liss, technical analyst with Sakura Dellsher. She called Friday's figures "significant," but for the short to medium term she was bearish. "I think the market is going to the September lows," she said. June T-bonds hit a low of 105-20/32 on September 5.
A T-bond futures trader noted that June T-bonds eked out a new high for the week in the quiet trade Thursday, but said "the market was just too short going into the report."
"No matter what, I still want to sell it," he added. "The question is do you want to sell them at higher or lower prices?"
Futures were unfazed early by a rise in the latest weekly jobless claims, which rose to 314,000 from 313,000, above the 310,000 forecast.

At the close, June T-bonds were up 2/32 at 107-20/32, 10-year notes up 3/32 at 105-27/32, munis rose 5/32 to 112-9/32, September bills rose 0.025 bps to 94.300, and September Euros rose 0.015 to 93.725. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
